quick_skim.title: Building a Nested LADDER for LLM Unstructured Post-Training Pruning
quick_skim.abstract: Non-uniform allocation can improve post-training pruning of large language models, yet quality can still degrade sharply at high sparsity. To control degradation as sparsity increases, we introduce LADDER (Layer-Wise Allocation via Damage-Driven Evaluation and Refinement), which allocates sparsity incrementally. At each step, it evaluates pruning an additional fraction of weights from each eligible layer and commits the layer update that causes the least end-to-end degradation per removed parameter. This process produces non-uniform sparsity profiles and exactly nested masks across multiple budgets. We evaluate LADDER on five OPT, Llama, and Qwen models across 10-90% sparsity, using SparseGPT as its candidate-generation backend and comparing against uniform and adaptive allocation baselines. Results reveal a clear operating-regime trade-off: LADDER is comparable or slightly weaker at benign sparsity but becomes substantially more robust from 70% onward. This high-sparsity advantage largely persists after posterior distillation across four of five models and translates into improved retention of aggregate zero-shot accuracy.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Introduces LADDER, a damage-driven incremental layer-wise sparsity allocation for post-training LLM pruning, producing nested masks across budgets; LLM compression but pruning, not quantization.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对大模型后训练剪枝在高稀疏度下质量骤降的问题，本文提出LADDER，按层逐步评估额外剪枝比例并以单位参数端到端退化最小为准提交层更新，从而生成非均匀稀疏剖面与跨预算严格嵌套的掩码。在五个OPT、Llama与Qwen模型10%至90%稀疏度上以SparseGPT为后端进行评测。该方法属于后训练剪枝压缩，与量化及视觉token压缩侧重不同。
quick_skim.llm_tldr: 针对大模型后训练剪枝在高稀疏度下质量骤降的问题，本文提出LADDER，按层逐步评估额外剪枝比例并以单位参数端到端退化最小为准提交层更新，从而生成非均匀稀疏剖面与跨预算严格嵌套的掩码。在五个OPT、Llama与Qwen模型10%至90%稀疏度上以SparseGPT为后端进行评测。该方法属于后训练剪枝压缩，与量化及视觉token压缩侧重不同。
quick_skim.matched_query_text: Papers central to 围绕 LLM/VLM 高效压缩与适配的研究检索关键词, especially work that connects or combines: post-training quantization techniques for large language models including GPTQ AWQ SmoothQuant and OmniQuant; joint quantization and low-rank adaptation for memory efficient fine-tuning of large models; applying orthogonal rotation or Hadamard transforms to reduce outlier effects in weight quantization; reducing the number of visual tokens in vision language models through pruning and merging; compressing video tokens while preserving temporal grounding and event detection; quantization sensitivity of visual and textual modalities in vision language models; How does orthogonal rotation affect the low rank structure of quantization error in large language models?; Can low rank adapters reconstruct quantization error after rotation better than before rotation?; What is the interaction between visual token pruning and post training quantization in vision language models?; How can we preserve temporal information when merging video tokens for video understanding models?.
